links.note: No link points at a blocked host (WhatsApp): the link's host (the text between https:// and the first :, /, ? or #, cut by hand, never a URL parser's host), lower-case and without a trailing dot, is refused when it equals an entry of blockedHosts or ends in "." + an entry. Telegram (https://t.me/…) is allowed as a contact link. Every reader checks appliesTo. On root.facebookUrl and root.instagramUrl (0.2.0 props, whose pattern allows more than a 0.3.0 link) 0.3.0 adds two rules, for pages checked against 0.3.0: every reader, the editor included, first refuses a value whose authority (between https:// and the first /, ? or #) holds @, %, a backslash or a non-ASCII character (no real Facebook or Instagram address does; URL parsers disagree on such a host), then the blocked hosts, on the host cut as above. The telegram button target is new in 0.3.0 for every CtaAction prop, the 0.1.0/0.2.0 buttons included (their notes predate it); it goes to root.telegramUrl.

notes.strictSince: Every block, prop and slot with "since" (added in 0.3.0 or later) is strict: a value that fails any keyword of its schema (pattern, lengths, item counts, enum, additionalProperties) is refused, and so is an unknown prop or item key on such a block. Props without "since" (0.1.0 and 0.2.0) keep their readers' older leniency.
notes.blockId: Every block's props.id: a string of 1–100 characters, unique across the whole tree.
notes.document: A page document holds root, content and zones. Blocks nest through slots only, so zones (Puck's DropZones, which no block uses) is absent or {}.
notes.patterns: A pattern matches the whole string under ECMA-262 rules ($ is the end of input): Python readers use re.fullmatch, Java readers Matcher.matches() or networknt's ECMA-262 regex. The 0.3.0 patterns use ASCII classes only, so the result is the same in every engine. `patterns` lists strings every reader must accept and refuse.
notes.liveData: ProductCards, AllProducts, About and VisitUs show live data (the Owner Portal's products and business facts), which the sites fill in only at the top level: no slot takes them.
notes.productsToShow: ProductCards and AllProducts store which products they show (source all, category or picked; category; productIds), never products: the site and the editor read the website's catalog per request and apply it. picked shows the productIds in their order; a picked product that was deleted or isn't published drops out; an unknown category shows no products. A missing prop means its default, today's behaviour. Project refuses a productIds entry new in the save that isn't a product of this website (field content[i].<Type>.productIds[j]). Their products and categories props are copies kept as stored for older readers.
notes.blockLimit: Blocks on the page in all, counting every block inside a container at every depth (40). Before 0.3.0 the top level was the only level.
notes.topLevelLimit: Blocks in the page's own content list, the top level (16).
notes.maxDepth: How deep blocks nest: a top-level block is depth 1, a block in its slot depth 2, a block in a slot of that one depth 3. Nothing sits deeper than 3, so a container at depth 3 stays empty.
notes.maxPerPage: Each component's maxPerPage counts its blocks at every depth, not only the top level.
notes.lastBlock: The Footer is the last block of the top level. Hero and Footer are topLevelOnly: never inside a container.
notes.slots: A container holds blocks in its slot props, each a list of blocks ({type, props}, as at the top level). A block in a slot must be allowed by it (allow "any": every type whose topLevelOnly is false, minus disallow), the slot holds minItems to maxItems blocks, and a slot with activeWhen holds blocks only while that prop has one of the listed values.
notes.uniqueBlockIds: Every block's props.id is unique across the whole tree, slots included.
notes.anchors: A Section's anchorId, when not empty, is unique on the page and never top, shop, visit, about, all-products (the site's own in-page link targets). Every other id the site emits holds a character the anchorId pattern can't (e.g. _), so the two never meet.
notes.links: A 0.3.0 link (Buttons items[].link, ImageBanner buttonLink, a rich text link's href) is a CtaAction target or an https:// address of the vetted pattern whose host page.links.blockedHosts doesn't block; never javascript:, data:, http: or a relative path. root.telegramUrl is https://t.me/<username> only.
notes.plainText: Every string is plain text, shown as text: no prop takes HTML, CSS, a script or an iframe. The only embeds are Video (YouTube, Vimeo) and Map (Google Maps embed), which the site builds from an address of the vetted pattern. A picture goes into CSS only as url("…") with the value CSS-escaped, never by string concatenation.

richText.note: Rich text is a restricted node tree in the TipTap/ProseMirror JSON shape (a subset of it), never HTML. A doc holds paragraphs, headings (attrs.level 2–4) and bullet or numbered lists; a list holds listItems, each holding paragraphs; paragraphs and headings hold text runs, each with optional marks: bold, italic, link (attrs.href: a CtaAction target or a vetted https:// address). Objects are strict: any other node, mark or key (class, style, target…) is refused. The site builds the elements itself.

notes.maxTextLength: The sum, over every text node of one RichText.body (paragraphs, headings and list items), of its text length in UTF-16 code units: JavaScript's length, Java's String.length(), Python's len(s.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2. At most 2000. JSON Schema's own maxLength counts code points, so a reader must count this one itself. One run may be as long as the whole tree, because ProseMirror merges neighbouring runs with the same marks.
notes.marksOncePerRun: A text run carries each mark type at most once: never two links, never bold twice (ProseMirror refuses such a run). The schema's uniqueItems only catches two equal marks; check the types.
notes.examples: Conformance trees: every reader accepts the valid ones and refuses the others; rule says which check refuses it (schema, maxTextLength or marksOncePerRun).

examples.name: two neighbouring runs with the same mark (ProseMirror merges them into one run of 1200)
2000 UTF-16 code units with emoji (999 emoji of 2 units and 2 letters)
2001 UTF-16 code units with emoji over two paragraphs (each run is fine; the tree is one unit too long)
a run with two link marks
a style key on a paragraph

images.note: Where each picture gets its alt text. required: a set picture (not null) with an empty alt doesn't save, unless decorativeProp is true. prop: an alt prop next to the picture; missing or empty uses the first non-empty fallback prop, as the site did before 0.3.0. optional: an alt prop; empty means decorative. fallback: no alt prop; the site uses this text. decorative: always alt="". "logos[].alt" is the alt of each item of logos; block root is the page root.

patterns.note: The value patterns new in 0.3.0, each with the props using it and strings every reader must accept and refuse with a whole-string match (ECMA-262; Python re.fullmatch, Java Matcher.matches()). The props' own schemas carry the same pattern; an empty string or a CtaAction keyword, where allowed, is another branch of the prop's schema.
